citations.quote: The minimum allotment for one- and two-person assistance groups is $24.
citations.source: FoodShare Wisconsin Handbook (WI DHS), 8.1.1 Income Limits

citations.quote: Most food units are considered broad-based categorically eligible if their gross monthly income is at or below 200% FPL
citations.source: FoodShare Wisconsin Handbook (WI DHS), 4.2.1 Categorical and Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility

citations.quote: Food units that include an elderly, blind or disabled (EBD) member with gross income over 200% of the FPL must be tested for FoodShare using the regular SNAP rules.
citations.source: FoodShare Wisconsin Handbook (WI DHS), 23-02 Version of 4.2.1 Categorical Eligibility

citations.quote: Except during an initial month, all eligible one-person and two-person households shall receive minimum monthly allotments equal to the minimum benefit.
citations.source: 7 CFR 273.10 Determining household eligibility and benefit levels

citations.quote: Categorically eligible assistance groups that include one or two persons are eligible for a minimum $24 allotment, except for the initial prorated benefit which cannot be less than $10.

citations.pinpoint: Minimum benefit, 48 States and DC; memo dated August 21, 2026
citations.quote: The minimum benefit for the 48 States and D.C. will increase to $25.
citations.source: USDA FNS, SNAP — Fiscal Year 2027 Cost-of-Living Adjustments (memo)

summary: The household is one person, age 85 and disabled, with monthly gross income of $2,581.83. That is just under Wisconsin's FY2026 200% FPL limit of $2,610, so the household is broad-based categorically eligible and no net income test applies. Net income is roughly $2,000–$2,200 a month, so 30% of it is far above the $298 one-person maximum and the computed benefit is $0. As an eligible one-person household it gets the $24 minimum instead: $24 × 12 = $288. The engine reaches the same result. Its net income ($2,036) differs from stage 1's ($2,214), but either figure gives the minimum benefit. The FY2027 $25 minimum comes from a USDA memo dated 2026-08-21, after the freeze, so $24 is the correct amount for Oct–Dec under frozen law. The consensus answer of $0 applies only the regular elderly/disabled 100% FPL net income test and misses Wisconsin's broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE).
